name: Nanning
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Nanning: China-ASEAN trade counterparties, Vietnam corridor supply chains and arbitration support.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters touching Nanning, scoped from Nashville: research on Chinese and Southeast Asian counterparties met through the China-ASEAN Expo and the Guangxi free trade zone, verification of suppliers and logistics firms on the Vietnam corridor, and factual support for counsel in China-ASEAN arbitration.
intro: Nanning is the capital of the Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region in southern China and presents itself as the country's main gateway to Southeast Asia. It lies near the Vietnamese border and is a node in the China-Vietnam economic corridor and the Western Land-Sea New Corridor. Since 2004 it has hosted the annual China-ASEAN Expo, which in 2024 drew exhibitors from across ASEAN and, for the first time, from Gulf and Shanghai Cooperation Organisation countries. Its economy combines trade and logistics with automotive manufacturing, aluminium processing, sugar, electronics and food processing. The Nanning Area of the China (Guangxi) Pilot Free Trade Zone covers 46.8 sq km, including a comprehensive bonded zone and areas for modern finance and the digital economy.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Nanning because so much China-ASEAN business is arranged, financed or disputed there. China-ASEAN trade reached 552 billion US dollars in the first seven months of 2024, and bilateral trade with Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Singapore each exceeded 100 billion dollars. Companies meeting distributors, suppliers and project partners at the Expo want to know who they are. Supply chains running overland to Vietnam raise questions about transshipment, origin claims and the logistics companies involved. Investors in the free trade zone's finance and cross-border e-commerce sectors need clarity on ownership. And parties to disputes seated in Nanning need documented facts for arbitration.

matters.title: China-ASEAN Expo counterparty research
matters.text: Background research on Chinese and Southeast Asian distributors, agents, suppliers and project sponsors met through the China-ASEAN Expo, covering registration, ownership, litigation, penalties, adverse media and sanctions screening in Chinese and ASEAN-language sources, so companies can assess counterparties before signing agreements or advancing payments.

matters.title: Vietnam corridor supply chain checks
matters.text: Testing the claims of manufacturers, traders and logistics companies moving goods between Guangxi and Vietnam, including who owns them, where processing actually takes place and whether related companies sit on both sides of the border, to help importers assess origin, transshipment and forced labour exposure.

matters.title: Cross-border e-commerce and finance partners
matters.text: Diligence on cross-border e-commerce platforms, payment intermediaries and finance companies registered in the Nanning free trade zone, covering shareholders, related parties, licences claimed, regulatory penalties and disputes, for partners and investors assessing integrity and regulatory risk.

matters.title: Arbitration and dispute support
matters.text: Assembling documented facts for counsel in disputes between Chinese and ASEAN parties, including arbitrations that may be heard in Nanning, by identifying the entities, controllers and related companies involved, their litigation history and their assets of record, to support claims and later enforcement.

matters.title: Agribusiness and commodity counterparties
matters.text: Background research on sugar, fruit, aluminium and other commodity traders and processors connected to Nanning, covering ownership, financial stress indicators, disputes and adverse media, so buyers, lenders and trade finance providers can judge counterparty reliability and the risk of duplicated or fictitious cargo documents.

local_context.title: CIETAC ASEAN centre in Nanning
local_context.text: The China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission opened an ASEAN-oriented centre in Nanning in August 2022. CIETAC may hear cases there where the arbitration clause names Nanning or Guangxi as the seat or where the parties agree, and the centre is intended to make Guangxi a regional arbitration hub for RCEP and ASEAN parties. Drafting and seat choices therefore affect where Nanning-related disputes are heard.

local_context.title: China-ASEAN arbitration cooperation centre
local_context.text: In September 2024 the China-ASEAN Commercial Arbitration Cooperation Center was inaugurated in Nanning during the China-ASEAN Commercial Law Forum. Initiated by the Guangxi arbitration association with the ASEAN Law Association, the Asian Institute of Alternative Dispute Resolution and other bodies, it is a non-profit cooperation platform rather than an administering institution, supporting exchange between Chinese and ASEAN arbitration bodies and arbitration services for regional trade.

local_context.title: Guangxi Pilot Free Trade Zone
local_context.text: The Nanning Area of the Guangxi Pilot Free Trade Zone covers 46.8 sq km in four functional areas: modern finance, intended as a model for financial openness to ASEAN; digital economy; culture, sports and health care; and processing trade and logistics, which includes the 2.37 sq km Nanning Comprehensive Bonded Zone. Entities registered in the zone may hold particular permissions, which diligence should confirm against actual operations.

local_context.title: Regional capital records
local_context.text: As Guangxi's capital, Nanning is the seat of the regional government and its departments, so regional administrative penalties and licensing decisions are important public records for counterparties in the city. We have not verified the specialised courts sitting in Nanning for this page; engagements identify the relevant court records, judgment databases and enforcement lists with the client's Chinese counsel before research begins.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Nanning, TDSC first establishes which side of each relationship sits in China and which in ASEAN countries, because counterparties met in Nanning often have owners, factories or bank accounts in Vietnam, Thailand or elsewhere. Research is conducted from Nashville using Chinese registration data, published judgments and administrative penalties, ASEAN company registries where available, and open sources in Chinese, English and Southeast Asian languages. Where site visits or local enquiries are justified, TDSC coordinates with qualified local professionals in China or the relevant ASEAN country and with the client's counsel. Personal information is collected only as needed, and any export of data from China is reviewed with counsel first.

faqs.q: How do we check a distributor we met at the China-ASEAN Expo?
faqs.a: We confirm the company's registration and status, identify its shareholders and related companies, and review litigation, enforcement records, administrative penalties and adverse media. For ASEAN-based counterparties we use the relevant national registry and local-language sources. We also run sanctions screening and flag where records are thin, so you can decide what further assurances to request.

faqs.q: Can TDSC verify a supplier shipping goods through Guangxi to or from Vietnam?
faqs.a: Yes. We research ownership on both sides of the border, compare stated production capacity and locations with public information, and look for related companies that may indicate transshipment or misdescribed origin. Where a factory visit is justified, we coordinate with qualified local professionals in China or Vietnam and the client's counsel.

faqs.q: Can arbitrations involving Chinese and ASEAN parties be heard in Nanning?
faqs.a: CIETAC opened an ASEAN-oriented centre in Nanning in 2022 and may hear cases there where the arbitration clause names Nanning or Guangxi as the seat or the parties agree. Whether a particular dispute belongs there is a question for counsel. We support counsel with factual research on the parties, their controllers and their assets.

faqs.q: What does diligence on a Nanning free trade zone company involve?
faqs.a: We review its registration, scope of business, shareholders and related parties, the permissions it claims, published judgments and administrative penalties, and its public footprint. For finance, payments and cross-border e-commerce businesses, we pay particular attention to regulatory penalties and to whether the company's actual activities match the zone permissions it relies on.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have an office in Nanning?
faqs.a: No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office or staff in Nanning or elsewhere in China or Southeast Asia. Most of our work is desk-based research. Where on-the-ground steps are needed, we coordinate with qualified local professionals acting lawfully and with the client's counsel, and we decline requests involving restricted records or covert methods.
